text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- The Confederation of Industry has asked health minister Yvonne Herloev Andersen to hold back implementing a parliamentary resolution to mark all genetically-engineered food products in retail stores. The confederation says that initial marking would cost the food industry 500 million crowns.

--- Copenhagen airport expects 175,000 flights between April-September 1997, an increase of 11 percent over last summer's traffic. The airport says that Turkey's Top Air and Base Airlines, of the Netherlands, are considering starting charter flights from Copenhagen in 1997.
--- A new survey by the National Statistics Office shows that 89 percent of Danes support current defence policy, including deployment of peacekeeping forces abroad.
--- Danish producers cannot meet consumer demand for ecological products and retailers now fear that they will be forced to buy from foreign suppliers.
--- The troubled Danyard shipyard hopes to survive on building advanced aluminium catamarans and chemical tankers in future.
